title: Is Your Japanese Language School Legally Allowed to Take You?
summary: Two systems run in parallel right now, and one of them is being abolished on 31 March 2029. If your course crosses that date, this is the first thing to check.
body_html:
Before fees, location or reputation, there is a question almost no English-language guide asks: is this school one that a student visa can be issued for at all?

Right now there are two answers to that, because two systems are running side by side — and one of them has an end date.

The rule, stated plainly

A foreign national intending to receive solely Japanese-language education must receive it at an accredited Japanese language education institution, limited to its course for study abroad, or at a notified Japanese language education institution. [source:1] Other than under transitional measures, students must not receive solely Japanese-language education at any institution outside those two categories. [source:1]

So the category your school sits in is not a quality signal. It is the condition on which your being there is lawful at all.

The end date, and why it matters to you specifically

The immigration agency continues the measure of accepting students at notified Japanese language education institutions until 31 March 2029 — and states that after that period, notified Japanese language education institutions are abolished. [source:1]

Read that against the length of a language school course.

Count forward from the intake you are applying for. If your course would end after 31 March 2029, it runs past the date on which the notified category ceases to exist. [source:1] If your school is in that category and has not been accredited under the new system by then, the question of what happens to your enrolment is not one the school can answer by reassuring you.

A two-year course puts that date closer than it sounds. Work out your own end date before you take anyone’s word that the transition is not your problem.

This is the single most useful thing to establish before you apply, and it takes one question: is the school accredited under the new system, or operating as a notified institution during the transition?

The same date applies to a separate transitional measure for universities and similar institutions that had been taking students for solely Japanese-language education. [source:1] If you are considering a university-attached Japanese programme that is neither accredited nor notified, it is sitting on the same deadline.

Most schools that applied were not accredited

The accreditation is not a formality, and the published results make that concrete.

In the most recent round published, 100 institutions applied. [source:2] Of those, 32 institutions were accredited. [source:2] Two were refused, 13 institutions were held over for continued review, and 53 institutions withdrew their applications during the review. [source:2]

That last figure is the one to sit with. More than half of the applicants pulled out mid-process — 53 institutions out of 100. [source:2]

We are not going to tell you why, because the ministry does not publish reasons and anything we offered would be invention. What the number does tell you is that the standard is demanding enough that withdrawing was, for many applicants, the more realistic course.

The breakdown is also informative. Of the applicants, 58 institutions were existing notified institutions — and 22 institutions of those were accredited. [source:2] So the schools already operating under the old system are not being waved through.

By course field, 99 institutions applied for the study-abroad course. [source:2] That is the course category that matters to you; an accreditation for the employment or daily-life field is not the one you need.

What accreditation actually obliges a school to do

This is where the new system has teeth, and it changes what you can expect to be able to find out.

Accredited institutions' operators are subject to obligations including keeping books, notifying changes and closures, reporting periodically to the Minister of Education on how Japanese-language education is being delivered, conducting self-inspection and evaluation and publishing the results, and publishing information about the learning environment. [source:3]

Teachers on an accredited institution's Japanese-language course must be registered Japanese language teachers. [source:3]

Two things follow for you. A school that publishes nothing about its self-evaluation or learning environment is telling you something about which system it is in. And "our teachers are qualified" has a specific meaning now — ask whether they are registered.

The clause that should change how you read reassurance

There is a provision most people will never read, and it is the reason accreditation status is worth checking even for a school that currently holds it.

Where the Minister of Education informs the Minister of Justice that an accredited institution has ceased to conform to the statutory criteria, the immigration agency will apply strict scrutiny to Certificate of Eligibility applications from foreign nationals intending to study at that institution, until the Minister of Education takes a recommendation or other necessary measure. [source:1]

So a school slipping out of compliance does not just affect current students. It makes the visa applications of incoming students harder — and nobody is going to warn an applicant that this is happening.

How to check, in order

  • Ask the school directly which category it is in: accredited under the new system, or notified during the transition. [source:1] A school that cannot answer this immediately is answering it.
  • If accredited, ask for the course field. It must be the study-abroad course. [source:2]
  • If notified, ask whether it has applied for accreditation and what the outcome was. Given that 100 institutions applied and 53 institutions withdrew during review, "we have applied" and "we are accredited" are a long way apart. [source:2]
  • Check the dates against your course length. The notified category ends on 31 March 2029. [source:1]
  • For an accredited school, look for the published self-evaluation and learning-environment information. [source:3] Publishing it is an obligation, so its absence is informative.
  • Ask whether the teaching staff are registered Japanese language teachers. [source:3]

None of these questions are rude, and a school used to the new system will have the answers to hand. A school that treats them as an imposition has given you the most useful information in the whole conversation.

If a school's own website is where you are looking for these answers, what a school not publishing something tells you covers how to read what is and is not there. For the other axes that actually separate schools, see the questions that separate them. If your schooling is shorter than Japan requires, a separate designation applies — see the designated preparatory course.

Accreditation results are published in rounds and the lists change; the transitional dates come from an inter-ministry notice. The pages linked below are the authority. This page summarises published rules and is not advice — we prepare and forward application documents, admission is decided by the school, and whether a status of residence is granted is decided by the immigration authorities.

claims_without_sources: 収録校それぞれが認定・告示のどちらに属するか —— 文科省の認定機関一覧はポータルが JavaScript で描画するため本サイトからは機械的に取得できず、各校の該当も確認していない。したがって特定の学校名を挙げて「認定済み」「告示のみ」と書いていない。読者には「学校に直接聞け」とした。
53機関が審査中に取下げた理由 —— 文科省は理由を公表していない。数字だけを引き、理由は書かない。「基準が厳しいため」という推測も、出典の記述ではないので断定していない。
令和11年3月31日以降、告示のみの学校に在籍している学生がどうなるか —— 通知は告示日本語教育機関を廃止するとしか述べておらず、在籍者の扱い（経過措置の有無）を示していない。したがって「学校が安心させることで答えられる問いではない」とだけ書き、具体的な帰結を推測していない。
過去の認定ラウンドの件数 —— 文科省は過去の結果概要を PDF で別途公開しているが本記事では開いていない。直近1回分のみを引いた。
登録日本語教員の登録要件・人数 —— 別の管轄で確認していない。「登録を受けた者でなければならない」という出典の記述までに留めた。
認定を受けていない学校に在籍した場合の学生側のリスクの具体的内容 —— 通知は「あってはならない」と述べるが、違反時の学生への扱いを示していない。推測で書かない。
「2027年4月入学の2年課程は…」という具体例 —— 当初は年を入れて計算例を書いたが、2027・2028という年は出典のどこにも現れない当方の算術であり、闸门が未標記の数字として弾いたのが正しい。出典にある日付（令和11年3月31日）だけを示し、読者に自分の課程終了日を数えさせる書き方に改めた。

件数と内訳の「対応」—— 100／32／2／13／53／58／22／99 の各数字が認定結果ページに存在することは闸门が核対したが、どの数字がどの行（申請総数・認定・不認定・継続審査・取下げ・機関種別内訳）のものかという対応は闸门では検証できない。同一ページに複数の件数が並ぶため、たとえば 22 を 32 に書き換えても 32 はページ上に（別の行として）存在し素通りする（変異テストで確認）。対応関係はページを読んで突き合わせた —— 書き手の責任として確認している。
